hypothesis: Low stock-specific return uncertainty may select better subsequent relative returns than momentum. Removing market-driven volatility should be compared with the simpler total-volatility ranking.
scope: Single-market daily log-return model in A shares; not a Fama-French replication or evidence that the published international result holds locally.
unique_change: Replace momentum ranking with minus the residual standard deviation from a trailing-252-session market OLS regression with intercept; smaller residual volatility ranks higher. Ordinary minus total return standard deviation over exactly the same valid pairs is a prespecified simpler control.
residual_sigma: sqrt(sum((r_i-mean(r_i)-beta*(r_m-mean(r_m)))^2)/(n-2)); OLS beta and all means use identical valid pairs, n>=120, positive market variance; total sigma uses sum((r_i-mean(r_i))^2)/(n-1). No annualization needed for ranks.
market_factor: Reuse the market-adjusted-strength adjacent-session SH/SZ equal-weight return series: finite positive closes, exclude abs(simple return)>0.5, average simple returns then log1p. Each signal uses only observations up to that date.
opportunities: Exactly 191688 archived eligible events in 82 month-end cross-sections; preserve all 284837 broad-reference rows, frozen 40-market-session outcomes, entry/exit costs, unfilled cash and censoring. No new momentum, trend, industry or volatility-level filter; no rematching.
unavailable_score_action: Stop with the full missing-score list; do not shrink the universe or impute zero volatility.
groups: Ten average-rank percentile bands with ties kept together. Highest score group selected; ordinary volatility and original momentum evaluated under the same opportunity/outcome contract.

statistics.weighting: equal signal months, equal allocations within group

reports: residual/total sigma, beta and observations for every eligible event
gross/net decile returns and Rank IC
annual top excess versus broad and matched references
paired improvement versus momentum and ordinary low volatility
selection overlap, replacement and mean beta
decision_rule: Apply the same training gates separately to both prespecified volatility rankings against momentum. If only one passes, retain it as a training candidate. If both pass, prefer ordinary low volatility unless residual volatility has positive paired-improvement CI lower bound versus ordinary low volatility. These are exploratory training comparisons, not independent or multiple-testing-adjusted confirmation.
pass_action: Validate the retained fixed ranking with an executable rebalance portfolio, turnover, drawdown, exposure and historical execution/issuer facts before any qualification.
fail_action: Stop both tested volatility representations and their lookback, percentile, holding-window, volatility-threshold and trend-filter neighbors. Move to a distinct selection mechanism; do not invert either ranking after seeing results.
